cards.title: Establish plan → structure → develop → audit → benchmark CI standard
cards.note: Define the standard pipeline every card-sized piece of work flows through, and wire it into the repo so it runs hands-off.
cards.help:
Goal: one declared pipeline — PLAN (spec the card), STRUCTURE (worktree +
files), DEVELOP (implement), AUDIT (ssot-validate, lint, tests),
BENCHMARK (measurable before/after) — that any card can opt into via
`pipeline: ci` and that kanban-dispatch runs hands-off.

Deliverables:
1. docs/ssot/ssot.ci.yml — stages, gates, required artifacts per stage
2. scripts/ci/ runner — executes a card through the stages, records
   stage results back into the card's comms
3. card_schema addition: `pipeline: ci` opt-in field
4. audit + benchmark wiring: pre-commit / timer / report node in
   ssot.reports.yml
5. a demonstration run on a real card
cards.spec:
Design and implement the standard Chaba CI pipeline for card-sized work:
plan → structure → develop → audit → benchmark.

Read first: docs/ssot/kanban/ssot.kanban.yml (card standard),
scripts/ssot-validate-all.mjs, scripts/ssot-optimize.mjs, the pre-commit
hook, and docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.reports.yml (report nodes).

Deliverables:
1. docs/ssot/ssot.ci.yml declaring the five stages, the gate that ends
   each stage, and the artifact each stage must produce.
2. scripts/ci/ — a runner that takes a card id, executes the stages it
   can automate, and writes stage results into the card's comms +
   a `pipeline:` status block. Gates it can't automate (e.g. Tony
   approval) become requests: entries on the card.
3. Card schema addition: `pipeline: ci` opt-in field (documented in
   ssot.kanban.yml card_schema).
4. Wire the audit stage to the existing validators; wire the benchmark
   stage to produce a before/after metric recorded on the card.
5. Demonstrate on one real small card.

cards.title: Cloudflare account + DNS for public edge
cards.note: DONE: api.surf-thailand.com proxied -> idc01 caddy -> ada-pi-pwa (200 via CF edge). idc01+edge records DNS-only. edge -> idc02. Optional: bump token scope to Zone Settings Edit to set SSL=strict (origin cert is valid LE).
cards.help:
1. dash.cloudflare.com → "Add site" → enter your domain → Free plan.
2. Cloudflare gives you 2 nameservers (e.g. ada.ns.cloudflare.com).
3. At your domain REGISTRAR → replace NS records with those two.
4. Wait for "Active" status on the CF dashboard (minutes to a few hours).
5. DNS → Records → add:
   A   idc01        <idc01 public IP — hardware-idc01-specs.md>   — see step 6
   A   <new-vps>    <its public IP>
6. Per record choose the cloud color:
   🟠 Proxied (orange) — only for real PUBLIC web endpoints (hides origin IP, adds WAF).
   ⚪ DNS only (grey)  — anything only tailnet/ssh should reach.
7. SSL/TLS → set "Full" (upgrade to "Full (strict)" once the origin serves valid TLS).
Optional later: `cloudflared` tunnel = public HTTPS with ZERO open ports on the VPS.
Done when: DNS resolves + you can say which records are proxied vs grey. Then idc-vps-game unblocks.

cards.title: Provision IDC VPS Game LG2SS+ (150GB) — edge+backups+monitor
cards.note: idc02 edge LIVE: caddy-edge quadlet on public 80/443 (ufw opened, sysctl unpriv ports=80). tony-ha + michael-ha proxied via CF -> 200. CF Access policy = remaining dashboard step (public now relies on HA auth alone).
cards.help:
Goal: LG2SS+ 150GB VPS → second public edge + offsite backup + external monitor.
1. Confirm CPU/RAM/disk in the provider panel (150GB is disk — get vCPU/RAM too).
2. Base hardening: apt update/upgrade, ufw allow 22/80/443, ssh keys only.
3. Join tailnet: `curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh | sh && sudo tailscale up`
   → host appears as a tailnet node (name it idc03 or similar).
4. Roles (in this order):
   edge    — Caddy on 80/443 proxying public domains → tailnet services
   backups — rsync/restic target receiving idc01 + tony-dell backups
   monitor — external uptime checks hitting idc01 + tony-dell health endpoints
5. Optional: third camwall pull edge.
Prereq: cloudflare-setup (DNS records must point at this host first).

cards.incident: 2026-10-03 21:24 — wedged on first big rotation (11.4GB binlog): health endpoint dead ~26min, process peaked 16.4GB RSS + 5.9GB swap, needed SIGKILL; mddb-gate held all Ada services down (user-visible outage). Rotation logic + memory bound needs fixing before promote.
cards.note: Janitor built + staged: image localhost/mddb:2.15.4-blrotate loaded on idc01. Needs leader restart (~2.5min open-rescan downtime, Ada memory errors meanwhile). Runbook: docs/kb/mddb-backup-binlog-2026-10-03.md.
cards.help: The binlog had MaxSize/MaxAge config that nothing enforced — grew 9.2G, ~1G/day. The janitor rotates past maxSize keeping from min follower ConfirmedLSN (age-cutoff when no followers). Smoke-tested; mddb-fork 598c57d on feat/vector-algorithms. Deploy: pin Image= in ~/.config/containers/systemd/mddb.container, daemon-reload, systemctl --user restart mddb. Rollback = point back at localhost/mddb:2.15.4-allowlist.

cards.title: Speaker-ID — verify KK voice hits are real voice, not TTS echo
cards.note: Session e564b39502 audio replay shows a genuine KK=0.84 match at t=0s — either KK spoke near the iPad, or Ada's own TTS / another device playing KK's voice leaked into the mic path. If no human KK was present, this is an echo-leak bug: self-voice or relayed audio reaching the recognizer. Owner- reclaim (f394a90 + d630572) now recovers the label in ~30s, but the false open still mis-greets. Also watch live identify logs for remaining sub-threshold owner sessions post re-enrollment.
cards.help:
1. Reproduce: start a voice session with no KK present, speak as Tony. 2. journalctl -u ada-ha-tony | grep identified — check first-chunk hits. 3. If false KK hits recur: check capture pipeline for TTS output bleeding
   back (see docs/ssot/ssot.learning.speaker-id-tts-echo.2026-10-03.yml).
4. Fix path would be AEC/echo suppression or ignoring speaker-id during
   Ada's own speech window.

cards.help:
1. git worktree list — classify each: merged / stale / active-session
2. git branch --merged master → delete merged branches (local + remote)
3. For branches ahead of master: either PR/merge, or archive label + remove
4. Worktrees belonging to dead sessions → git worktree remove
5. Re-run reports/DEV_SYSTEM_ASSESSMENT — cons should drop to 0
